subject: MayaTech evaluation playbook & next steps for structured output testing
summary: Post-discovery follow-up: recommended model candidates, benchmark links, JSON schema compliance strategy, proposed tool-calling session and task list for a canary eval.
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@mayatech.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@mayatech.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:02:00Z
Subject: MayaTech evaluation playbook & next steps for structured output testing

Hi Maria / Jorge —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Highlights from discovery:
- Primary use case: ingest customer support transcripts, extract structured incident objects (customer_id, intent, category, severity, suggested_resolution) and pass to downstream ticketing API.
- SLOs: 95th p99 gen latency < 450ms for 512-token requests, JSON-schema conformance >= 99% success, and retry behavior for transient failures.
- Data constraints: PII redaction required; MayaTech prefers us to run initial evals in us-east region and avoid cross-region copies.

Recommended model candidates (for the canary eval):
- redwood-instruct-7b-quant (fast, good structured-output baseline)
- redwood-flan-13b (higher quality on instruction-following — keep as secondary for PR-recall checks)
- open-70b-llm-quant (reserve for high-quality check only; will increase latency/cost).

Evaluation plan (short):
1) We run a 1k-example canary on your sample transcripts (attached prompt_set + schema) and produce: token-level latency pkgs, JSON-schema pass/fail, top-5 hallucination/regression checks.
2) We instrument function/tool-calling tests: call the ticketing API stub (local sandbox) for successful parses; for schema failures we attach a structured error that triggers our retry policy (exponential backoff x3) with a fallback to a lighter parsing model.
3) Deliverables: eval_kpi_snapshot.csv, examples of failures + prompts to reproduce, and suggested batching/quantization profile for production.

Next steps I propose this week:
- You: share sample export (10–100 transcripts) and an anonymization pass we can run (or permission for us to run redaction).
- Us: schedule a 60-minute toolcall to run the canary + live function-calling test.
- Internal: we’ll prep prompt_set_v1 and structured_output_schema_v2 (attached) and pre-stage the three model variants in us-east.

Attachments included: mayatech_prompt_set_v1.json, structured_output_schema_v2.json, eval_kpi_snapshot.csv (template).

Tentative slot: tomorrow 09:30–10:30 ET — I posted a Cal link below; if that doesn’t work, give a couple of alternate times and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to running the canary.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@mayatech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@mayatech.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T18:47:00Z
Subject: Re: MayaTech evaluation playbook & next steps for structured output testing

Thanks Hannah — great summary and thumbs up on the approach. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data / residency: we will provide a 50-record anonymized export this afternoon. Can you confirm the canary will run in us-east-1 only and that no copies will leave that region?
2) JSON compliance: our engineers require a strict schema check. When you say >=99% success, what is the failure handling path? We prefer a deterministic fallback (attempt a 2nd parse, then tag as manual-review).
3) Retries: network retries are fine, but for model-parsing retries we want to ensure idempotency (the ticketing API sandbox accepts an idempotency_key); can you incorporate that in the function-call tests?

Also, can you share the exact prompt examples you’ll use for the canary so we can sanity-check them versus our internal annotations?

We’re good on the proposed slot tomorrow 09:30 ET. Please send the invite.

Best,
Maria Ortiz
Director, Product Integrations | MayaTech

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T20:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: MayaTech evaluation playbook & next steps for structured output testing

Looping in Ben for commercial/contract considerations and to confirm we can run the canary under existing NDA:

Ben — this is a qualified mid-market prospect (MayaTech) — deal_id MT-2027-042. Key asks: us-east only evaluation, JSON-schema failure path (2 parses then manual review), idempotency on function calls.

Action items for Ben:
- Confirm commercial guardrails for a free canary (I recommend 2,000 tokens total per customer for the canary under our eval credits).
- If they request a DocuSign for a temporary evaluation Addendum, please send the template.

Action items for Hannah:
- Prep the exact prompt variants we’ll run (happy to review before we send to MayaTech).
- Pre-stage redwood-instruct-7b-quant and redwood-flan-13b in us-east and allocate a small dedicated slot for repeatable timing measurements.

I’ll join the call tomorrow 09:30 ET to help take notes on commercial asks.

— Sergio
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@mayatech.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@mayatech.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: MayaTech evaluation playbook & next steps for structured output testing

Thanks Maria — appreciate the quick confirmation. A few concrete deliverables before the toolcall: 

1) Prompt pack: attached (mayatech_prompt_set_v1.json) — includes positive controls, adversarial examples, and a short rubric to evaluate regression.
2) Schema enforcement: structured_output_schema_v2.json — if the model output fails schema check we will run a second parse with the lighter redwood-instruct-7b-quant (deterministic seed + nucleus sampling tuned) and if still failing we will tag the record for manual review. That path includes adding idempotency_key to the function-call payload so your sandbox dedups.
3) Retry policy: we will use exponential backoff (200ms, 500ms, 1s) for transient 5xx or network failures. Model-parse retries are counted separately (max 1 model-parse retry).

I created a calendar invite for tomorrow 09:30–10:30 ET and a short runbook in Drive with the evaluation checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MayaEvalPlaybook. Please accept; if you prefer a different time, ping me.

If you can upload the anonymized sample to that Drive folder we’ll pick it up before the meeting.

Looking forward to it.

—
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Attachments: mayatech_prompt_set_v1.json, structured_output_schema_v2.json, eval_kpi_snapshot.csv
